transcription.notes: One-page problem list for the 30th IYPT 2017 (released July 4th, 2016); 17 problems printed, matching the inventory count of 17 (the inventory title list stops at 12). No points, no time limit and no solutions are printed. The page also carries an epigraph (Isaac Newton), an author list, the problem selection committee, figure and epigraph credits, and an electronic-signature box; these are not part of any problem. The grey horizontal bar printed beside the start of problem 7 belongs to the problem 6 figure (the horizontal surface under the chain) and is included in that crop. No text was changed.

problems.title: Invent Yourself
problems.statement: Construct a passive device that will provide safe landing for an uncooked hen’s egg when dropped onto a hard surface from a fixed height of 2.5 m. The device must fall together with the egg. What is the smallest size of the device you can achieve?

solution.incompleteReason: IYPT problems are open research problems; no official solutions are published.

problems.title: Balloon Airhorn
problems.statement: A simple airhorn can be constructed by stretching a balloon over the opening of a small container or cup with a tube through the other end (see Figure). Blowing through a small hole in the side of the container can produce a sound. Investigate how relevant parameters affect the sound.

figures.alt: Sketch of the airhorn: a cup whose open end is covered by a stretched membrane, with a tube passing through the other end into the cup (dashed inside); a small blow hole in the side. Labels: Blow hole, Tube, Membrane, Cup.

problems.title: Leidenfrost Stars
problems.statement: In the Leidenfrost effect, a water drop placed on a hot surface can survive for minutes. Under certain circumstances, such a drop develops oscillating star shapes. Induce different oscillatory modes and investigate them.

problems.title: Fast Chain
problems.statement: A chain consisting of wooden blocks inclined relative to the vertical and connected by two threads (see Figure) is suspended vertically and then released. Compared to free fall, the chain falls faster when it is dropped onto a horizontal surface. Explain this phenomenon and investigate how the relevant parameters affect the motion.

figures.alt: A vertical chain of six inclined bars (wooden blocks) joined by two vertical threads; the bars alternate in tilt direction. A downward arrow on the right indicates the direction of fall; a grey horizontal bar below the chain represents the horizontal surface.
